|- | No. 203 Kofun || {{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is [[Category:pp error]]approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, forming a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge forming a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, forming a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun formed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat forming a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which forms a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 forms a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was formed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no artifacts were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is designated No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to form a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear[[Category:pp to pp]] to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to form on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the formation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * Parking lot == Brief History of Investigations and Maintenance == * April 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered the Mukaizan Subgroup of the Kawada kofun group * May 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and the Nanonomiya Subgroup * July 1976: Mound survey of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society and the Archaeological Research Association of {{ill|Kanazawa University|ja|金沢大学}} * 1988: Excavation survey of Shirohama Naburayama No.1 Kofun conducted by the Nanao City Board of Education during factory site development * 1994: The kofun group in Toriya Town was designated a historic site by the town. * 1995–1996: Distribution surveys and small-map_size test excavations conducted by the Toriya Town Board of Education aimed at park development for the designated historic site * 1995: Ground-penetrating radar survey of Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by the {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} stretching from the former {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).

|- | No. 203 Kofun || {{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is [[Category:pp error]]approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, forming a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge forming a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, forming a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun formed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat forming a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which forms a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 forms a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was formed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no artifacts were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is designated No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to form a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear[[Category:pp to pp]] to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to form on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the formation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * Parking lot == Brief History of Investigations and Maintenance == * April 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered the Mukaizan Subgroup of the Kawada kofun group * May 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and the Nanonomiya Subgroup * July 1976: Mound survey of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society and the Archaeological Research Association of {{ill|Kanazawa University|ja|金沢大学}} * 1988: Excavation survey of Shirohama Naburayama No.1 Kofun conducted by the Nanao City Board of Education during factory site development * 1994: The kofun group in Toriya Town was designated a historic site by the town. * 1995–1996: Distribution surveys and small-map_size test excavations conducted by the Toriya Town Board of Education aimed at park development for the designated historic site * 1995: Ground-penetrating radar survey of Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by the {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} stretching from the former {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).

|- | No. 203 Kofun || {{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is [[Category:pp error]]approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, forming a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge forming a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, forming a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun formed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat forming a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which forms a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 forms a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was formed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no artifacts were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is designated No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to form a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear[[Category:pp to pp]] to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to form on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the formation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} stretching from the former {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).
{{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] In the 1990s, the distribution of the Kawada Souyama and Kawada Nanonomiya subgroups was examined in detail「表7～10」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) (excluding tumulus-like uplifts). |- | No. 203 Kofun || {{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is [[Category:pp error]]approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, forming a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge forming a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, forming a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No artifacts were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun formed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat forming a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which forms a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appear[[Category:pp to pp]]s somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 forms a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was formed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no artifacts were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is designated No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of [[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to form a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun ([[Category:pp error]]approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear[[Category:pp to pp]] to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to form on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the formation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * Parking lot == Brief History of Investigations and Maintenance == * April 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered the Mukaizan Subgroup of the Kawada kofun group * May 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and the Nanonomiya Subgroup * July 1976: Mound survey of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by members of the City Board of Education during factory site development * 1994: The kofun group in Toriya Town was designated a historic site by the town. * 1995–1996: Distribution surveys and small-map_size test excavations conducted by the Toriya Town Board of Education aimed at park development for the designated historic site * 1995: Ground-penetrating radar survey of Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by the {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} stretching from the former {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).
{{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] In the 1990s, the distribution of the Kawada Souyama and Kawada Nanonomiya subgroups was examined in detail「表7～10」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) (excluding tumulus-like uplifts).
