{{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社|12=draft}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, typeing a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge typeing a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appears to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, typeing a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun typeed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat typeing a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appears to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which types a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appears somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代|12=draft}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 types a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was typeed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression (approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no burial goods were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is Historic Site1 No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to type a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun (approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun (approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun (approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun (approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群|12=draft}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to type on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the typeation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun|12=draft}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} stretching from the typeer {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町|12=draft}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|12=draft}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島|12=draft}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市|12=draft}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun|12=draft}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).

{{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社|12=draft}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, typeing a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge typeing a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appears to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, typeing a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun typeed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat typeing a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appears to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which types a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appears somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代|12=draft}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 types a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was typeed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression (approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no burial goods were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is Historic Site1 No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to type a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun (approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun (approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun (approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun (approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群|12=draft}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to type on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the typeation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun|12=draft}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} stretching from the typeer {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町|12=draft}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県|12=draft}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島|12=draft}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市|12=draft}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun|12=draft}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. {{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社|12=draft}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, typeing a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge typeing a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石|12=draft}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appears to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, typeing a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun typeed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat typeing a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appears to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which types a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appears somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代|12=draft}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 types a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was typeed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression (approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no burial goods were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is Historic Site1 No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to type a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun (approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun (approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun (approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun (approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun|12=draft}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群|12=draft}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to type on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the typeation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun|12=draft}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} stretching from the typeer {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).

|- | No. 203 Kofun || {{ill|enfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || 10 || 0.1–0.8 || Possibly natural terrain |} == Major Kofun == === Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun === [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|3DCG rendering of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun}}]] Trench excavations for boundary confirmation were carried out in 1999 and 2000「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the southeast File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the front of the anterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the posterior portion File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the northwest File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCG rendering, viewed from the side ==== Kofun (Mound) Characteristics ==== Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun is located at the southwestern end of a 140‑m long ridgeline behind {{ill|Hakusan Shrine|ja|白山神社}} and is constructed with its posterior portion facing the plain. The elevation of the posterior part is about 40 m, and the relative height from the foot of the hill is approximately 25 m. Due to soil extraction, part of the posterior mound has been lost. It cleverly utilizes natural terrain; the anterior portion’s front is cut from the ridgeline’s saddle, typeing a terraced flat surface from the anterior to the posterior part along the south side of the mound, which is presumed to have originally continued to the very rear. In contrast, the northern side of the posterior part transitions into a natural hillside, and only a right‐angled triangular flat surface can be discerned between the northern side of the anterior part and the posterior part. The mound shows slight distortion, with the front end of the anterior portion not perpendicular to the main axis but with a projecting northern corner. Also, the posterior part is not square, with the main axis being short and the rear edge typeing a slightly broad trapezoid. The top of the posterior mound is broadly flat. The anterior portion shows a slight rise at its tip. It is built in two tiers: in the posterior part, the upper tier is constructed with embankment, while the lower tier is cut from the natural hill; a step is also presumed at the front end of the anterior part due to differences in mound slope. The upper tier is overall angular. No peripheral moat was detected at the mound’s edge. No {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} or {{ill|fukiishi|ja|葺石}} were observed 「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). According to the results of the above excavation survey, the mound measures as follows: total length 55.0 m, posterior part length 30.5 m, central width of posterior part 36.1 m, height from the southern foot 5.0 m, constricted part width 13.1 m, anterior part tip width 25.0 m, and anterior part tip height 3.3 m . ==== burial goods ==== Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} were recovered from the flowing soil in various trenches on the southern side of the posterior part, presumed to belong to the associated kofun . Fragments of {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} were unearthed from the trench floor at the constricted part on the southern side; these small fragments make precise dating difficult 「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」 『石川考古 第254号』 石川考古学研究会 (1999). ==== built ==== The first academic report on this kofun, published in 1977 in 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』, dated it to the 5th century. This was based on the recovery of 6th century early Sue pottery from Souyama No.5 Kofun and the orderly arrangement of kofun Nos. 2–10 relative to No.1, suggesting a close relationship between them . The 1978 publication 『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 also dates it to the 5th century 「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』 鹿西町教育委員会 (1978). After further excavation, the 2001 publication 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』, comparing it with other zenpō-kōhōfun and keyhole-shaped kofun in Noto, and noting its tiered construction, re-dates it to the mid-4th century to the third quarter (contemporaneous with the Amagomiya No.1 Kofun) . === Kawada Souyama No.2 Kofun === A round kofun constructed slightly lower than the northwestern corner of No.1 Kofun. Its peripheral moat runs along the slightly trimmed slope at the foot of No.1 Kofun. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.4 Kofun === A medium-sized round kofun constructed adjoining the rear of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun on its western slope. Its type is ovate; the peripheral moat appears to have significantly disturbed the terrace of No.1 Kofun’s posterior part, typeing a linear type along the portion adjoining the mound edge. No burial goods were recovered; dating is unknown . === Kawada Souyama No.5 Kofun === Located southwest of Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun. Although the top has been flattened for cemetery construction, it is considered a round kofun with a diameter of approximately 15 m. From the trimmed surface, four fragments of pottery (including a neck fragment and a jar neck fragment) were collected; these are estimated to belong to the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Souyama No.6 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun typeed by cutting into the southwestern corner of No.1 Kofun, with its peripheral moat typeing a half-circle. The moat on the eastern side of the mound is excavated 0.5 m into the base of No.1 Kofun. The mound appears to have been built by adding 0.7 m of fill adjacent to No.1 Kofun’s base. Sue pottery jar fragments were found at the bottom of the moat, displaying features of the TK47 type (late 5th century, 4th quarter), and are presumed to be associated with this kofun . Additionally, fragments of pottery of the TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter) were found floating in the moat, suggesting that Souyama No.7 Kofun may be the source . === Kawada Souyama No.7 Kofun === A small, low round kofun constructed on the terrace of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A large tree on its summit has collapsed, damaging the mound . === Kawada Souyama No.8 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. A round kofun constructed on the southeastern slope by cutting from the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. A half-circular moat exists on its northern half. Excavations recovered eight fragments of Sue pottery (such as broken pieces) from the bottom of the moat, estimated as MT85 or TK43 type (late 6th century). This kofun is considered the most recent among those confirmed in the group . === Kawada Souyama No.23 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1999. Located on the top of the posterior part of No.1 Kofun. Excavation revealed an irregular elliptical earthen embankment; 15 large and small pebbles were recovered from the center. Although presumed to be a tomb, its nature remains unclear. built is unknown . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.31 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Located on the ridgeline at the western end of the hill. Although it is a round kofun, its proximity and connection to No.30 Kofun (which types a keyhole type) suggest that together they may constitute a zenpō-kōhōfun; excavation revealed that a trench was cut perpendicular to the ridge between No.31 and No.30, confirming that No.31 is a round kofun while No.30 is a remnant mound. No peripheral moat exists; a terraced flat surface extends from the west to the north. The summit is wide but appears somewhat flattened. A trench beneath the associated ditch yielded a 0.6‑m wide ditch thought to date to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代}} . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.32 Mound === Trench survey conducted in 1998. Adjoins the northwestern foot of No.31 Kofun. Excavations confirmed the existence of a peripheral moat around the mound; a {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowl was recovered from the moat bottom. The back side features a cord-marked surface, suggesting a date from the 10th–ppth century or later. Compared to the kofun, its summit is rounded in a bun-shaped manner. Similar morphology in nearby Nos. 91, 61, and 62 indicates that it is a mound . === Kawada Nanonomiya Nos. 47–48 Kofun === Trench survey conducted in 2000. Located nearly centrally on the hill’s ridgeline. No. 47 is a stratified round kofun, while No. 48 types a low mound. To determine whether No. 48 is a mound or a kofun, a trench was excavated between them; Sue pottery jar fragments were recovered from the summit of No. 48, identified as TK208 type (mid-5th century, 3rd quarter), leading to its classification as a round kofun . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.74 Kofun === Trench surveys conducted in 1996 and 1997. Located on a subsidiary ridgeline on the southern slope of the western end of the hill. It is a medium-sized round kofun constructed by cutting off the rear of the adjoining ridge. Excavations revealed that the northern half of the mound was shaped by reworking the natural hill, while the southern half was typeed by fill. Additionally, an irregular depression (approximately 3.8 m wide, 9 m long, and at least 0.6 m deep) is observed, presumed to be a grave pit; no burial goods were recovered . === Kawada Nanonomiya No.93 Kofun? === Trench survey conducted in 1995. A complete high-sided Sue pottery shard was recovered from the trench. The terrain shows a tumulus-like uplift, and the artifact may have fallen from above; for convenience, it is Historic Site1 No.93 Kofun. It is an uncovered high mound with a single-tier leg, displaying features of the MT15 type (early 6th century) . === Kawada Mukaizan Subgroups === ==== Subgroup A (Kawada Mukaizan A) ==== Located at the westernmost end of the hill. These mounds are densely distributed along the gently spreading ridge and its gentle slope adjoining the mound bases. All the mounds are small, with diameters of approximately 5–10 m and heights around 1 m; from external observation, 50 mounds were confirmed. Three mounds constructed at the foot of the hill are exposed in cross-section on a cut face, but no stone chamber or coffin usage is observed . Their distribution was re-surveyed by the Toriya Town Board of Education in the 1990s 「表pp～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). ==== Subgroup B (Kawada Mukaizan B) ==== 25 mounds were confirmed. They tend to type a linear distribution along a ridgeline, centered on relatively large round kofun (approximately 15 m in diameter and about 2 m high), grouped in units of 7–10 mounds into three small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup C (Kawada Mukaizan C) ==== 20 mounds were confirmed. They show a distribution similar to subgroup B and can be divided into 2–3 small subgroups . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup D (Kawada Mukaizan D) ==== 27 mounds were confirmed. Located on a high ridge, centered on a relatively large round kofun (approximately 20 m in diameter and about 3 m high), with smaller round kofun (approximately 5–10 m in diameter) distributed along a branching subsidiary ridge in units of 4–7, which can be divided into 5 small subgroups based on their distribution . Re-surveyed in the 1990s by the Toriya Town Board of Education . ==== Subgroup E (Kawada Mukaizan E) ==== Distributed on a tongue-shaped ridge extending eastward from the ridge where subgroup D is located, across the saddle. 17 mounds were confirmed. A relatively large round kofun (approximately 18 m in diameter and about 2.5 m high) stands at the highest point, with smaller mounds arranged linearly along branching ridges in three to four small subgroups (each comprising 4–6 mounds) . ==== Subgroup F (Kawada Mukaizan F) ==== Situated about 100 m apart from subgroup D across the hill’s saddle. 18 mounds were confirmed. They exhibit a distribution similar to subgroups B and C and appear to divide into roughly 3–4 small subgroups . ==== Subgroup G (Kawada Mukaizan G) ==== Confirmed 3 mounds on a hillside slightly below the main ridgeline. They possess relatively high mounds for their small diameters, and the internal structure may include a horizontal tunnel–style stone chamber. A group of horizontal tunnel–style kofun in the Shirohama area exists on the northern mid-slope of the same hill, drawing attention to possible connections between them . Also known as the Shirohama Naburayama Kofun Group. No.1 Kofun in this subgroup is a round kofun with a diameter of 13.5 m, a wooden coffin interment, from which Sue pottery (jar + teppin) and Haji pottery (a bowl with a handle and a long-neck jar) were recovered; it is dated to the late 6th century 『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』 七尾市教育委員会 (1989). == Historical Context Surrounding the Kawada Kofun Group == In the Noto region, various zenpō-kōhōfun are found, with tiered construction evident in examples such as the {{ill|Yanagida Fuo-yama Kofun|ja|柳田布尾山古墳|1=Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun}}, {{ill|Amagomiya Kofun Group|ja|雨の宮古墳群|1=Amenomiya Kofun Cluster}}, and Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun. Based on the features of tiered construction, the mound type of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun—characterized by its tiered structure, flat surfaces at the mound’s base, and constricted upper tier—can be seen as similar to Amagomiya No.1 Kofun, suggesting a contemporaneous construction period . Prior to the construction of Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun, large-map_size kofun such as those in the {{ill|Oda Chūko Kofun Group|ja|小田中古墳群}} and the Amagomiya Kofun Group began to type on the Noto Peninsula. At that time, the central area of the alluvial plain in the Ochi region was the most productive agricultural area, equidistant from both the outer and inner harbors, and also strategically positioned to control maritime routes from the Ninomiya River basin to the west coast of the inner bay. The interred individual of Souyama No.1 Kofun was likely a chieftain playing a significant role in Noto’s political power, and his lineage may have been connected to or descended from the family associated with Otsuki No.pp Kofun, Kokubu Amizuka No.1 Kofun, Oda Nakagame Kamezuka Kofun, and Amagomiya No.1 Kofun 「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」 『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001). After the construction of Souyama No.1 Kofun, there was a gap of about one century before the typeation of later {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}, which continued unbroken in the Kawada Souyama, Kawada Nanonomiya, and Kawada Mukaizan A–D subgroups from the third quarter of the 5th century to the late 6th century. In these subgroups, no evidence of stone chambers was found in the burial facilities. Horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers became widespread in smaller kofun in Noto only from the fourth quarter of the 6th century; therefore, these subgroups can be regarded as cluster kofun predating the generalization of horizontal tunnel–style stone chambers, and they eventually declined during the latter half of the 6th century . == Kofun Park Toriya == Located at the northwestern foot of the Souyama subgroup and adjacent to Ōike to the west, this park was established with the following features {{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや|accessdate=2020-05-05}}: * 26,900 m² of Fureai Park * 28,700 m² of Waterfront Park * Playground * One pavilion for rest * One observation tower * Boat dock * Barbecue facilities * Parking lot == Brief History of Investigations and Maintenance == * April 1976: Members of the Ishikawa Archaeological Society discovered the Mukaizan Subgroup of the Kawada kofun group * May 1976: excavations conducted by the Toriya Town Board of Education aimed at park development for the Historic Site1 historic site * 1995: Ground-penetrating radar survey of Souyama No.1 Kofun conducted by [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|[[3DCG]]で描画した川田ソウ山1号墳}}]] 1999年・2000年に範囲確認のためのトレンチ発掘を実施「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。南東方向から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。前方部正面から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。後方部から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。北西方向から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。真横から見る ==== 墳丘 ==== 川田ソウ山1号墳は白山神社裏の長さ140mの丘陵尾根の南西端に位置し、後方部を平野に面して築造されている。後方部の標高は約40m、丘陵裾からの比高は約25mを測る。土砂採集により後方部後方の墳丘が失われている。 自然地形を巧みに利用しており、前方部前端は丘陵鞍部を切断したもので、墳丘南側に前方部から後方部にかけてテラス状の平坦面が形成されており、本来後方部後方まで続いていたと推定される。一方、後方部北側は自然の丘陵斜面に移行しており、前方部北側と後方部の間に直角三角形状の平坦面を認めるに過ぎない。 墳丘はやや歪みが認められ、前方部前端は主軸に直交せず北角が突出している。また後方部は正方形ではなく、主軸方向が短く、後辺部にやや広い台形状をなす。後方部墳頂は平坦面が広い。前方部は先端が若干隆起する。2段築成をなし、後方部では上段が盛土、下段は地山削り出しで墳丘を整えている。前方部前端にも墳丘傾斜の違いから段が想定できる。上段が全体として鋭角的である。 墳端に周溝を検出できなかった。[[埴輪]]・[[葺石]]は認められない「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 上記発掘調査の成果による墳丘規模は以下の通り。全長55.0m、後方部長30.5m、後方部中央幅36.1m、高さ南裾より5.0m、くびれ部幅13.1m、前方部前端幅25.0m、前方部前端高さ3.3m。 ==== 出土遺物 ==== 後方部南側の各トレンチで流土中等から[[須恵器]]片若干が出土したが周囲の古墳に伴うものと判断される。くびれ部南側トレンチ床面から[[土師器]]片が出土。小片なので時期判別は難しい「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」『石川考古　第254号』石川考古学研究会（1999年）。 ==== 築造年代 ==== 本墳を最初に学術的に報告した1977年刊行の『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』では、本墳を5世紀代としていた。ソウ山5号墳から6世紀前半の須恵器が出土し、1号墳に対する2～10号墳の整然とした配置からそれらの古墳と1号墳の間に密接な関係が予想されたからである。 1978年刊行の『雨の宮古墳群の調査』「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』鹿西町教育委員会（1978年）でも5世紀代としている。 発掘調査を経て2001年に刊行された『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』では、能登近辺の前方後方墳・前方後円墳との比較検討、段築を有することなどから、4世紀中頃から第3四半期（雨の宮1号墳とほぼ同時期）に比定している。 === 川田ソウ山2号墳 === 1号墳北西角からやや降ったところに築造された円墳。1号墳裾下の斜面をやや削って周溝がめぐっている。出土遺物なく時期不明。 === 川田ソウ山4号墳 === 1号墳後方部後方に接して西斜面に築造された中規模円墳。墳形は卵形をなし、同墳周溝は1号墳後方のテラスをかなり損ねているとみられ、墳端に接する部分で直線的となっている。出土遺物なく時期不明。 === 川田ソウ山5号墳 === 川田ソウ山6号墳の南西に位置する。墓地造営のため頂上が削平されているが径約15mの円墳と考えられる。削平された面よりはそう頸部片、甕頸部片など4点の土器片が採集されている。MT15型式（6世紀前半）に属するものと推定。 === 川田ソウ山6号墳 === 2000年にトレンチ調査を実施。1号墳南西角を切って周溝を半周させた円墳。周溝幅は墳丘北で狭く、東側で広がる。墳丘東側の周溝は1号墳裾を0.5m掘り込んでいる。墳丘は1号墳裾に0.7m盛土を施すものであった。周溝底より須恵器甕片が見つかり、TK47型式（5世紀第4四半期）の特徴を持ち、出土状態からみて本墳にともなうものであろう。 他に周溝中に浮いた状態で出土したTK208型式（5世紀第3四半期）と考えられる土器片があり、その流出元としてソウ山7号墳が候補と考えられる。 === 川田ソウ山7号墳 === 1号墳後方部テラス上に築造された小形低墳丘の円墳。墳頂の大木が倒れて墳丘が損なわれている。 === 川田ソウ山8号墳 === 2000年にトレンチ調査を実施。1号墳後方部南東角を切って南斜面に築造された円墳。北半分に周溝が半周している。発掘の結果、周溝底から坏等の須恵器8片が出土、MT85ないしTK43型式（6世紀後半）と推定される。本古墳は古墳群中で確認された中で最も新しい時期に属する。 === 川田ソウ山23号塚 === 1999年にトレンチ調査を実施。1号墳後方部墳頂にあり。発掘調査の結果、不整形な楕円形の土壙が検出。中央に大小15個の礫石が出土。墓と推定されるが性格はよくわからない。築造年代は不明。 === 川田七ノ宮31号墳 === 1998年にトレンチ調査を実施。丘陵西端の尾根頂上に位置する。円墳であるが方丘をなす30号墳と接していることから合わせて前方後円墳となる可能性があり、発掘調査を実施。結果は30号墳との間に尾根に直交して溝が掘られており、31号墳は円墳、30号墳は残丘であることが判った。他の部分に周溝はなく、西から北にかけてテラス状の平坦面が形成されている。墳頂部は広いがやや削平されているようである。 古墳に伴う溝の下から[[弥生時代]]後期と思われる幅0.6mの溝が検出。 === 川田七ノ宮32号塚 === 1998年にトレンチ調査を実施。31号墳墳裾北西に接する。発掘調査の結果、本塚をめぐる周溝が確認され、溝底に[[土師器]]碗が出土。裏は糸切底となっており10～11世紀以降に下るものと考えられる。古墳と比べて頂上が丸く饅頭状をなす。付近にある91号、61号、62号も同じ形態をなしているので塚と判断した。 === 川田七ノ宮47号墳・48号墳 === 2000年にトレンチ調査を実施。丘陵尾根のほぼ中央に47・48号墳がある。47号墳は成層的な円墳であるが、48号墳は低墳丘をなしている。後者が塚であるか否かを探るため、両墳間にトレンチ発掘を実施、48号墳墳頂から須恵器甕片が出土。TK208型式（5世紀第3四半期）と考えられ、48号墳も円墳と判断された。 === 川田七ノ宮74号墳 === 1996・1997年にトレンチ調査を実施。丘陵西端斜面の南側支脈尾根に位置する中規模円墳。背後の尾根を断ち切って造営。発掘調査の結果、墳丘の北半部を地山整形、南半部に盛土を施していることが判った。また南北方向に幅3.8m、長さ9m、深さ0.6m以上のやや不整形な墓壙とみられる落ち込みが検出。遺物等は出土していない。 === 川田七ノ宮93号墳？ === 1995年にトレンチ調査を実施。トレンチから完形の須恵器高坏1点が出土。地形は墳丘状隆起であり、上から転落してきた遺物とも考えられるが、便宜上93号墳とする。長脚一段透かしの無蓋高坏で、MT15型式（6世紀前半）の特徴を有する。 === 川田向山A支群 === 丘陵最西端部に位置する。なだらかに広がる尾根上とその緩傾斜面に墳裾を接するように密集して分布する。墳丘のすべては径5～10m前後、高さ1m前後の小規模低墳丘のもので、外面的な観察で確認されたものは50基。丘陵裾で造墓されたもの３基が切通面に墳丘断面を露呈しているが、石室・石棺などの使用は認められない。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている「表11～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 === 川田向山B支群 === 25基を確認。比較的規模の大きい円墳（径15m前後、高さ2m前後）を中心に尾根筋状に列状に分布する傾向。7～10基を単位に3小支群にまとまりをみせる。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている。 === 川田向山C支群 === 20基を確認。B支群と同様の分布傾向を示し、2～3小支群に分割可能。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている。 === 川田向山D支群 === 27基を確認。尾根高所に位置する比較的規模の大きい円墳（径約20m、高さ約3m）を中心にヒトデ状に分岐する支尾根に径5～10m級の円墳が4～7基を1単位としてまとまりをみせる。分布状況からみて5小支群に分けられる。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている。 === 川田向山E支群 === D支群が立地する尾根とは鞍部を挟んで東に舌状に拡がる丘陵尾根上に分布する。17基を確認。最高所に立地する位置する比較的規模の大きい円墳（径約18m、高さ2.5m）を中心に3方向に分岐する尾根筋状に列状に分布、4～6基を1単位に3～4小支群よりなるものとみられる。 === 川田向山F支群 === D支群と丘陵鞍部を挟んで約100m隔てている。18基を確認。B・C支群と同様の分布状況を呈し、およそ3～4の小支群に分かれそうである。 === 川田向山G支群 === 尾根筋からやや降った丘陵斜面で3基を確認。小規模な墳径に比較して高い墳丘を持ち、内部主体は横穴式石室である可能性もある。同一丘陵北端部の中腹に白馬横穴群が存在しており、本支群との関連が注目される。 白馬ナブラ山古墳群ともいう。1号墳は径13.5mの円墳で木棺直葬、須恵器（甕+提瓶）と土師器（把手付椀・長頸壺）が出土し、6世紀末の年代とされている『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』七尾市教育委員会（1989年）。 == 川田古墳群を取り巻く歴史的環境 == 能登周辺の前方後方墳で、段築は[[柳田布尾山古墳]]、[[雨の宮1号墳]]、川田ソウ山1号墳に認められる。川田ソウ山1号墳は段築・墳裾平坦面・上段くびれ部の特徴からみて雨の宮1号墳に近い墳丘型式ということができ、築造年代も前後するものと推定される。 川田ソウ山1号墳造営の前段階において、能登半島では大規模古墳を主墳とする[[小田中古墳群]]や雨の宮古墳群などの形成が始まっており、能登の政治勢力の中枢が地溝帯中部域に集中化しつつあった。邑知沖積地の中央部で農業生産力の最も高い地域であり、外浦・内浦の海運拠点とも等距離の位置に当たる。そして北部能登への接触にも便利な二宮川流域から西湾岸へのコースを掌握する地域でもあった。 ソウ山1号墳の被葬者はおそらく能登の政治勢力の一翼を担うものであり、その出自として挙げられるのは大槻11号墳・国分尼塚1号墳・小田中亀塚古墳・雨の宮1号墳の被葬者の近親者もしくはこれを祖とする一族の長と考えられる「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 川田ソウ山1号墳築造後、約1世紀の空白期間を経て後期[[群集墳]]の形成が始まる。少なくとも川田ソウ山支群・川田七ノ宮支群・川田向山A～D支群では5世紀第3四半期から6世紀後半まで途切れることなく築造されている。これらの支群では埋葬施設に石材を使用した形跡はみられない。能登の小規模墳に横穴式石室が普及するのは6世紀第4四半期からであり、これらの支群は横穴式石室が一般化する以前の群集墳ということができ、6世紀後半のうちに消長するものといえる。 ==古墳公園とりや == ソウ山支群の北西裾、大池西隣に開園。主な内容は下記{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.town.nakanoto.ishikawa.jp/life_service_local/3/3/1960.html |title=中能登町古墳公園とりや |accessdate=2020-05-05 }}。 * ふれあい公園26,900平方メートル * 水辺公園28,700平方メートル * 遊具広場 * 休憩棟 1棟 * 展望台 1棟 * ボート乗り場 * バーベキュー施設 * 駐車場 == 調査と整備小史 == * 1976年4月：石川考古学研究会会員により川田向山支群の古墳群が発見される * 1976年5月：石川考古学研究会会員により川田ソウ山1号墳および七ノ宮支群の古墳群が発見される * 1976年7月：石川考古学研究会と[[金沢大学]]考古学研究会により川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘測量が実施される * 1988年：工場敷地造成工事に係り白馬ナブラ山1号墳が七尾市教育委員会により発掘調査される * 1994年：鳥屋町町内の古墳群が町指定史跡となる * 1995～1996年：鳥屋町教育委員会により史跡指定公園整備をめざし分布調査・小規模試掘を実施 * 1995年：マイアミ大学地球物理学応用考古学探査研究所によりソウ山1号墳の地中レーダー探査を実施「付章　地中レーダー探査」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年） * 1997年：七ノ宮74号墳のトレンチ調査 * 1998年：七ノ宮30～32号墳のトレンチ調査 * 1999～2000年：川田ソウ山1号墳および周囲の古墳のトレンチ調査 == 位置情報 == {{座標一覧}} * {{国土航空写真}}1975年。]] '''川田古墳群'''（かわだこふんぐん）は、[[能登半島]]中央部、[[石川県]][[鹿島郡]][[中能登町]]（旧[[鳥屋町]]）から[[七尾市]]にまたがる[[古墳]]の集まりをいう。[[前方後方墳]]である川田ソウ山1号墳と[[群集墳]]からなる。 川田ソウ山1号墳（前方後方墳）を含むソウ山支群、七ノ宮支群、川田向山A～G支群の9支群に分かれる。 * 川田ソウ山支群：23基。1998年に精査、墳丘状隆起を含む「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年） * 川田七ノ宮支群：61基。1997年に精査、墳丘状隆起を含む * 川田向山A～G群：約170基『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』石川考古学研究会（1977年） == 構成内容 == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|ソウ山支群・七ノ宮支群分布図（空中写真に重ね合せ）。
{{国土航空写真}}1975年。]] 1990年代に分布が精査された、川田ソウ山支群・川田七ノ宮支群について構成内容を記す「表7～10」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。ただし墳丘状隆起は除く。 * 前方後方墳1基 * [[円墳]]60基 * 塚5基 * 墳丘状隆起18基 ===川田ソウ山支群=== {| class="wikitable" ! 名称 !! 墳形 !! [[File:CG_K_Souyama_1_3_7p.jpg|thumb|right|250px|{{center|[[3DCG]]で描画した川田ソウ山1号墳}}]] 1999年・2000年に範囲確認のためのトレンチ発掘を実施「第2章　調査の方法」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 File:CG_K_Souyama_1_1_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。南東方向から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_7_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。前方部正面から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_4_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。後方部から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_5_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。北西方向から見る File:CG_K_Souyama_1_6_7p.jpg|3DCGで描画。真横から見る ==== 墳丘 ==== 川田ソウ山1号墳は白山神社裏の長さ140mの丘陵尾根の南西端に位置し、後方部を平野に面して築造されている。後方部の標高は約40m、丘陵裾からの比高は約25mを測る。土砂採集により後方部後方の墳丘が失われている。 自然地形を巧みに利用しており、前方部前端は丘陵鞍部を切断したもので、墳丘南側に前方部から後方部にかけてテラス状の平坦面が形成されており、本来後方部後方まで続いていたと推定される。一方、後方部北側は自然の丘陵斜面に移行しており、前方部北側と後方部の間に直角三角形状の平坦面を認めるに過ぎない。 墳丘はやや歪みが認められ、前方部前端は主軸に直交せず北角が突出している。また後方部は正方形ではなく、主軸方向が短く、後辺部にやや広い台形状をなす。後方部墳頂は平坦面が広い。前方部は先端が若干隆起する。2段築成をなし、後方部では上段が盛土、下段は地山削り出しで墳丘を整えている。前方部前端にも墳丘傾斜の違いから段が想定できる。上段が全体として鋭角的である。 墳端に周溝を検出できなかった。[[埴輪]]・[[葺石]]は認められない「第3章　調査の記録」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 上記発掘調査の成果による墳丘規模は以下の通り。全長55.0m、後方部長30.5m、後方部中央幅36.1m、高さ南裾より5.0m、くびれ部幅13.1m、前方部前端幅25.0m、前方部前端高さ3.3m。 ==== 出土遺物 ==== 後方部南側の各トレンチで流土中等から[[須恵器]]片若干が出土したが周囲の古墳に伴うものと判断される。くびれ部南側トレンチ床面から[[土師器]]片が出土。小片なので時期判別は難しい「鳥屋町川田ソウ山1号墳の墳丘調査」『石川考古　第254号』石川考古学研究会（1999年）。 ==== 築造年代 ==== 本墳を最初に学術的に報告した1977年刊行の『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』では、本墳を5世紀代としていた。ソウ山5号墳から6世紀前半の須恵器が出土し、1号墳に対する2～10号墳の整然とした配置からそれらの古墳と1号墳の間に密接な関係が予想されたからである。 1978年刊行の『雨の宮古墳群の調査』「第6章　雨の宮古墳群の歴史的意義」『雨の宮古墳群の調査』鹿西町教育委員会（1978年）でも5世紀代としている。 発掘調査を経て2001年に刊行された『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』では、能登近辺の前方後方墳・前方後円墳との比較検討、段築を有することなどから、4世紀中頃から第3四半期（雨の宮1号墳とほぼ同時期）に比定している。 === 川田ソウ山2号墳 === 1号墳北西角からやや降ったところに築造された円墳。1号墳裾下の斜面をやや削って周溝がめぐっている。出土遺物なく時期不明。 === 川田ソウ山4号墳 === 1号墳後方部後方に接して西斜面に築造された中規模円墳。墳形は卵形をなし、同墳周溝は1号墳後方のテラスをかなり損ねているとみられ、墳端に接する部分で直線的となっている。出土遺物なく時期不明。 === 川田ソウ山5号墳 === 川田ソウ山6号墳の南西に位置する。墓地造営のため頂上が削平されているが径約15mの円墳と考えられる。削平された面よりはそう頸部片、甕頸部片など4点の土器片が採集されている。MT15型式（6世紀前半）に属するものと推定。 === 川田ソウ山6号墳 === 2000年にトレンチ調査を実施。1号墳南西角を切って周溝を半周させた円墳。周溝幅は墳丘北で狭く、東側で広がる。墳丘東側の周溝は1号墳裾を0.5m掘り込んでいる。墳丘は1号墳裾に0.7m盛土を施すものであった。周溝底より須恵器甕片が見つかり、TK47型式（5世紀第4四半期）の特徴を持ち、出土状態からみて本墳にともなうものであろう。 他に周溝中に浮いた状態で出土したTK208型式（5世紀第3四半期）と考えられる土器片があり、その流出元としてソウ山7号墳が候補と考えられる。 === 川田ソウ山7号墳 === 1号墳後方部テラス上に築造された小形低墳丘の円墳。墳頂の大木が倒れて墳丘が損なわれている。 === 川田ソウ山8号墳 === 2000年にトレンチ調査を実施。1号墳後方部南東角を切って南斜面に築造された円墳。北半分に周溝が半周している。発掘の結果、周溝底から坏等の須恵器8片が出土、MT85ないしTK43型式（6世紀後半）と推定される。本古墳は古墳群中で確認された中で最も新しい時期に属する。 === 川田ソウ山23号塚 === 1999年にトレンチ調査を実施。1号墳後方部墳頂にあり。発掘調査の結果、不整形な楕円形の土壙が検出。中央に大小15個の礫石が出土。墓と推定されるが性格はよくわからない。築造年代は不明。 === 川田七ノ宮31号墳 === 1998年にトレンチ調査を実施。丘陵西端の尾根頂上に位置する。円墳であるが方丘をなす30号墳と接していることから合わせて前方後円墳となる可能性があり、発掘調査を実施。結果は30号墳との間に尾根に直交して溝が掘られており、31号墳は円墳、30号墳は残丘であることが判った。他の部分に周溝はなく、西から北にかけてテラス状の平坦面が形成されている。墳頂部は広いがやや削平されているようである。 古墳に伴う溝の下から[[弥生時代]]後期と思われる幅0.6mの溝が検出。 === 川田七ノ宮32号塚 === 1998年にトレンチ調査を実施。31号墳墳裾北西に接する。発掘調査の結果、本塚をめぐる周溝が確認され、溝底に[[土師器]]碗が出土。裏は糸切底となっており10～11世紀以降に下るものと考えられる。古墳と比べて頂上が丸く饅頭状をなす。付近にある91号、61号、62号も同じ形態をなしているので塚と判断した。 === 川田七ノ宮47号墳・48号墳 === 2000年にトレンチ調査を実施。丘陵尾根のほぼ中央に47・48号墳がある。47号墳は成層的な円墳であるが、48号墳は低墳丘をなしている。後者が塚であるか否かを探るため、両墳間にトレンチ発掘を実施、48号墳墳頂から須恵器甕片が出土。TK208型式（5世紀第3四半期）と考えられ、48号墳も円墳と判断された。 === 川田七ノ宮74号墳 === 1996・1997年にトレンチ調査を実施。丘陵西端斜面の南側支脈尾根に位置する中規模円墳。背後の尾根を断ち切って造営。発掘調査の結果、墳丘の北半部を地山整形、南半部に盛土を施していることが判った。また南北方向に幅3.8m、長さ9m、深さ0.6m以上のやや不整形な墓壙とみられる落ち込みが検出。遺物等は出土していない。 === 川田七ノ宮93号墳？ === 1995年にトレンチ調査を実施。トレンチから完形の須恵器高坏1点が出土。地形は墳丘状隆起であり、上から転落してきた遺物とも考えられるが、便宜上93号墳とする。長脚一段透かしの無蓋高坏で、MT15型式（6世紀前半）の特徴を有する。 === 川田向山A支群 === 丘陵最西端部に位置する。なだらかに広がる尾根上とその緩傾斜面に墳裾を接するように密集して分布する。墳丘のすべては径5～10m前後、高さ1m前後の小規模低墳丘のもので、外面的な観察で確認されたものは50基。丘陵裾で造墓されたもの３基が切通面に墳丘断面を露呈しているが、石室・石棺などの使用は認められない。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている「表11～12」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 === 川田向山B支群 === 25基を確認。比較的規模の大きい円墳（径15m前後、高さ2m前後）を中心に尾根筋状に列状に分布する傾向。7～10基を単位に3小支群にまとまりをみせる。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている。 === 川田向山C支群 === 20基を確認。B支群と同様の分布傾向を示し、2～3小支群に分割可能。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている。 === 川田向山D支群 === 27基を確認。尾根高所に位置する比較的規模の大きい円墳（径約20m、高さ約3m）を中心にヒトデ状に分岐する支尾根に径5～10m級の円墳が4～7基を1単位としてまとまりをみせる。分布状況からみて5小支群に分けられる。 1990年代に鳥屋町教育委員会により分布が再調査されている。 === 川田向山E支群 === D支群が立地する尾根とは鞍部を挟んで東に舌状に拡がる丘陵尾根上に分布する。17基を確認。最高所に立地する位置する比較的規模の大きい円墳（径約18m、高さ2.5m）を中心に3方向に分岐する尾根筋状に列状に分布、4～6基を1単位に3～4小支群よりなるものとみられる。 === 川田向山F支群 === D支群と丘陵鞍部を挟んで約100m隔てている。18基を確認。B・C支群と同様の分布状況を呈し、およそ3～4の小支群に分かれそうである。 === 川田向山G支群 === 尾根筋からやや降った丘陵斜面で3基を確認。小規模な墳径に比較して高い墳丘を持ち、内部主体は横穴式石室である可能性もある。同一丘陵北端部の中腹に白馬横穴群が存在しており、本支群との関連が注目される。 白馬ナブラ山古墳群ともいう。1号墳は径13.5mの円墳で木棺直葬、須恵器（甕+提瓶）と土師器（把手付椀・長頸壺）が出土し、6世紀末の年代とされている『七尾市埋蔵文化財調査報告9　白馬ナブラ山1号墳』七尾市教育委員会（1989年）。 == 川田古墳群を取り巻く歴史的環境 == 能登周辺の前方後方墳で、段築は[[柳田布尾山古墳]]、[[雨の宮1号墳]]、川田ソウ山1号墳に認められる。川田ソウ山1号墳は段築・墳裾平坦面・上段くびれ部の特徴からみて雨の宮1号墳に近い墳丘型式ということができ、築造年代も前後するものと推定される。 川田ソウ山1号墳造営の前段階において、能登半島では大規模古墳を主墳とする[[小田中古墳群]]や雨の宮古墳群などの形成が始まっており、能登の政治勢力の中枢が地溝帯中部域に集中化しつつあった。邑知沖積地の中央部で農業生産力の最も高い地域であり、外浦・内浦の海運拠点とも等距離の位置に当たる。そして北部能登への接触にも便利な二宮川流域から西湾岸へのコースを掌握する地域でもあった。 ソウ山1号墳の被葬者はおそらく能登の政治勢力の一翼を担うものであり、その出自として挙げられるのは大槻11号墳・国分尼塚1号墳・小田中亀塚古墳・雨の宮1号墳の被葬者の近親者もしくはこれを祖とする一族の長と考えられる「第5章　古代能登半島と川田古墳群」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』鳥屋町教育委員会（2001年）。 川田ソウ山1号墳築造後、約1世紀の空白期間を経て後期[[群集墳]]の形成が始まる。少なくとも川田ソウ山支群・川田七ノ宮支群・川田向山A～D支群では5世紀第3四半期から6世紀後半まで途切れることなく築造されている。これらの支群では埋葬施設に石材を使用した形跡はみられない。能登の小規模墳に横穴式石室が普及するのは6世紀第4四半期からであり、これらの支群は横穴式石室が一般化する以前の群集墳ということができ、6世紀後半のうちに消長するものといえる。 {{国土航空写真}} 1975.]] '''Kawada Kofun Group''' (かわだこふんぐん) refers to the collection of {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} stretching from the typeer {{ill|Toriya Town|ja|鳥屋町}} in {{ill|Nakanoto Town|ja|中能登町}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|ja|石川県}}, across central {{ill|Noto Peninsula|ja|能登半島}} to {{ill|Nanao City|ja|七尾市}}, comprising a group of kofun including the {{ill|zenpō-kōhōfun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} Kawada Souyama No.1 Kofun and a cluster of {{ill|gunshūfun|ja|群集墳|1=Gunshufun}}. Kawada Kofun Group is divided into nine subgroups: * **Kawada Souyama Subgroup:** 23 mounds. Surveyed in 1998; includes tumulus-like uplifts 「第4章　川田古墳群の検討」『石川県鳥屋町川田古墳群』 鳥屋町教育委員会 (2001) * **Kawada Nanonomiya Subgroup:** 61 mounds. Surveyed in 1997; includes tumulus-like uplifts * **Kawada Mukaizan A–G Subgroup:** Approximately 170 mounds 『鳥屋・高階古墳群分布調査報告』 石川考古学研究会 (1977) == Composition == [[File:Kawada Shichinomiya & Souyama.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Distribution map of the Souyama and Nanonomiya subgroups (superimposed on an aerial photograph).
